description: Conformance vectors for the numeric model ruled 2026-09-08 (gastownhall/bdp#21): groups of admissible spellings that denote one exact decimal value and therefore compare equal under the no-op law, with the RFC 8785 serialization every member of a group shares; admissible boundary literals; literals refused at admission because their exact decimal value does not round-trip through binary64, each with the shortest form the nearest binary64 serializes to; and three properties documents — two admissible respellings of one value with the sha256-jcs digest they share, and one refused at a nested member. Literals are carried as JSON strings so their spellings survive parsing. Illustrative vectors; not evidence.
rule: A number literal is admissible if and only if converting its exact decimal value to the nearest IEEE 754 binary64 value and serializing that value back in its shortest round-trip form (ECMAScript Number::toString, RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3) yields a literal denoting the same exact decimal value. Two admissible literals are the same value if and only if their exact decimal values are equal.

sameValue.note: Exact decimal values have no signed zero: -0.0 denotes zero, converts to binary64 negative zero, and serializes as 0 (RFC 8785 Appendix B, minus zero) — the same value as 0 (NM1).
The exponent respellings and the expanded 301-digit form gastownhall/bdp#21 asked about are one value.

admitted.note: 2^53 itself is representable: the boundary is representability, not magnitude.
2^53 + 2 is representable; only the odd integers past 2^53 are not.
Not exactly representable in binary64, yet admissible: the nearest binary64 serializes back to 0.1.
The smallest positive binary64 (RFC 8785 Appendix B).
The largest binary64 (RFC 8785 Appendix B); the exponent respelling denotes the same value.

refused.reason: An integer past 2^53: the nearest binary64 is 2^53, which serializes back to a different exact value.
Twenty significant digits: no binary64 serializes back to them.
Twenty significant digits spelling the binary64 nearest 0.1 more exactly than 0.1 does; that binary64's shortest round-trip form is still 0.1, a different exact value.
2^64 - 1, the integer RFC 7493 Section 2.2 recommends carrying as a JSON string.
Beyond binary64 magnitude — RFC 7493 Section 2.2's own example — so there is no finite binary64 to serialize.

documents.note: Every literal is admissible. jcs is the RFC 8785 serialization of the document; sha256Jcs is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of those UTF-8 bytes — what a scheme named sha256-jcs digests. The token encoding a scheme applies to that digest is the scheme's own.

admitted-document with every number respelled as another admissible spelling of the same value and its members reordered: the same exact values, the same RFC 8785 bytes, the same sha256-jcs digest — written over admitted-document, a no-op.
Refused at admission for the one inadmissible literal, at depth; pointer is the JSON Pointer of the offending member within properties, which the write profiles' diagnostic names. Nothing changes.
